I'm an amateur photographer who primarily uses Adobe Lightroom and Adobe Photoshop for post.  Occasionally I'll use a standalone product for a specific effect, but I'd say 99% of my work is done in Lightroom/Photoshop.  I've been frustrated with many company's switch to subscription based products (like Adobe Creative Cloud and Microsoft Office 365), and have been looking for alternatives.
Recently I have started using Darktable and Pixeluvo as Lightroom/Photoshop replacements and have found them to be very efficient and effective.  I can do post on hundreds of images quickly with excellent results and rarely find myself missing features of their more expensive competition.
As for Pixeluvo, I really like the interface.  It is modern, fast and clean.  The dialog boxes for effects and such work extremely well and show very fast previews of what they will render.  It can also handle RAW files, which is a huge plus.  Basic photography workflow is typically opening, cropping/rotating, brightness/contrast, color saturation/temperature, resizing and sharpening for output.  While a digital asset management program like Lightroom or Darktable is engineered specifically for working with large numbers of digital photographs and are very efficient at doing so, image editing programs like Photoshop and Pixeluvo are essential for individual image manipulation, especially where more technical work needs to be done such as with layers and compositioning.
I've only had one minor issue wth Pixeluvo on linux.  I'm currently running Linux Mint 17 Cinnamon 64bit and for some reason when opening images within Pixeluvo, the highlighted file selected in the open dialog dissappears while selected.  You can still open it, and if you mouse or keyboard to another file, it shows the previously selected file, but it is odd.  I contacted the developer and they promptly investigated and replied saying they could reproduce the bug and are now looking into it.  They said it was something specific to the Steam version as the standalone version did not show the same error.  They even gave me a new license key for the standalone version, and they were correct, the file open bug is absent.
When traveling and editing photos, I like to take my Acer C720 Chromebook, which has a Haswell CPU and 4GB of memory.  The SSD has been upgraded to 128GB drive, and the ChromeOS replaced with Linux Mint.  For doing basic tasks, this very cheap computer with the SSD and running linux seems just as fast as my i5 an i7 systems.  Obviously it has its limitations, but for quick and dirty content creation is certainly can do the job.  Pixeluvo running on this system takes around 51MB of RAM and launches in around 2 seconds and uses 43.9MB of drive space.  Darktable also launches in about 2 seconds and uses 110MB of RAM and uses less than 1MB of drive space.  I do have Lightroom 5.2 and Photoshop CS6 installed on this system also with WINE and in comparison Photoshop launches in 8 seconds, uses 216MB of RAM and takes up 470MB of drive space, with Lightroom launching in 7 seconds, using 103MB of RAM and takes 920MB of drive space.  The well programmed Pixeluvo and Darktable are small, fast and efficient at their tasks with their expensive competition the opposite.
I highly recommend this software.

How should I describe Paladins? It certainly isn't a B-TEC Overwatch, and the hate it recieves definitely isn't warranted.
I'm going to start this review by comparing it to Overwatch, since that seems needed.
-Paladins obviously contains similar gameplay mechanics to Overwatch, does it copy Overwatch? No. If anything, Overwatch copies Team Fortress 2... What I'm trying to say is, these kind of games take inspiration from eachother, and as a market, isn't that what games do? (and have always done?)
-In some places, this game is better than Overwatch. It has quality of life additions, such as mounts which greatly improve the flow of the game, and of course the pace. The problem with Overwatch is that it is very slow to get back into the game after dying.
-Overwatch certainly looks better than Paladins, but Paladins is a free to play title. That's the best part, it's free.
-Paladins has it's own unique, thought-out characters that all feel different to play.
-The competitive scene is big.
You lose nothing by trying this title, and I assure you if you like team based games you will most probably like this one.

At this time I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone except the most die-hard space 4x fans. I want to love the game. I really do. I've played it a lot but most of my time has been bug-fixing. Fixing typos, errors, and what can only be described as sloppiness. It feels like I'm beta-testing a game and trying to patch the game myself. I've tried to push through this, but even ignoring all of the bugs and crashes gameplay itself is shallow. Civ5 has much deeper gameplay. GalCiv3's gameplay is just so simple. When you get down to it, past all of the glitter, it feels almost like a mobile game. There just isn't a lot of depth to the game.
If you are a die-hard 4x fan and can't get enough turn based space games, then go for it.
The rest of you? Stay far, far away. GalCiv3 in its current state is a bug riddled, bloated, crashy, unstable mess. Expect your game to crash to desktop without any warning or error messages. Fortunately it has autosave, but there are so many stability problems that you're going to need those autosaves.
To start with, the positives. The game is gorgeous. It looks so very pretty. The ship designer is amazing. You can design almost any ship you want, anything from an Imperial Star Destroyer to one of Starfleet's finest. The level of customization is immense. The game is also very easy to mod as it is based on xml files, so tinkering is easy. All you need is notepad.
Unfortunately I've now finished the list of positive aspects of the game.
The game is riddled with typos, both spelling errors visible in the game as well as typos in the xml files that run the game behind the scenes. Research buildings are flagged as factories. Ship blueprints are poorly written, so that ships will be built with the wrong ship modules or missing vital ship modules entirely. This also leads to a very poorly performing AI because it is stuck with the stock ships. You can design your own ships, and by designing a well balanced ship you will be able to smash the AI.
To make up for this, at high difficulty levels the AI blatantly cheats. This game doesn't have an advanced AI. Its only made challenging by cheating. The AI ignores fog of war. It gets free production, free money, and free science. Its ships get more range and can install more modules than you. It also outright gets free technology every few turns. It needs all of these things to keep pace with a human player, and even then, the AI isn't much of a challenge except for sheer brute force due to cheating.
The AI isn't clever. It appears to pick a random planet to attack. It builds lots of ships and keeps flying it at that planet until it gets lucky. Unfortunately the AI forgets to build any transports on a regular basis, so it has trouble actually capturing planets. Diplomacy with the AI is very limited. You can trade things with the AI and you can declare war/peace with the AI. Thats about it. Want to get one AI to form an alliance with another AI? Can't do it. You can ally with everyone but you cannot broker peace in the galaxy. The AI's diplomacy is also mostly based on power. Do you have the most ships? Everyone loves you. Do you have the weakest fleet out of everyone? Everyone hates you and will declare war on you. Thats about as fancy as the AI gets.
The game is immensely bloated. 6gb of RAM isn't recommended. 6gb of RAM is barely the minimum. The game can use upwards of 5gb of RAM just by itself. Windows is going go use anywhere from 2-3gb of RAM. You need at least 6gb of RAM free. Not installed, but free/unused RAM. So you're looking at 10-12 of installed RAM to properly play this game.
In terms of visuals the game sure is pretty, but its pretty on par with Civ5. Its a turn based strategy game. However the memory usage far exceeds that of Civ5. Your computer may be able to play Civ5 without a hitch, but its going to crawl on GalCiv3. For some reason the game uses vast amounts of system resources (mostly memory) but it doesn't use them efficiently in an way. Expect your page file to get a lot of work. Your virtual memory is just a swap file on your hard drive. This file is going to get a ton of usage due to the memory requirements for this game. Hard drives are very slow things and virtual memory is to be avoided at all costs due to its terrible performance. Well, for GalCiv3, thats just what happens. Expect to chug along, especially if you're trying to play on a bigger map.
Management of your empire in game is also a chore. It chugs along. There is zero macro-management and zero automation. You have to micromanage every single planet, starbase, fleet, and ship in your empire every turn. On a tiny map its tolerable, but on big maps? Its micro management hell. And its not the fun kind of micro management. Its pure busywork. Its pure tedium. Starbases are particularly bad. They require a staggering degree of babysitting. Even planets, if you have a lot of them, get bad. There is no way to automate any planets in your empire. On a big map you might have dozens or potentially even hundreds of planets on the biggest map size. Every single planet must be manually ordered to do everything. Its just not fun. It is absolutely tedious.
That said, negatives aside, the game has a lot of potential, but it feels like I'm playing an early beta build. Its just so rough. The game feels so unfinished. This game is not ready for release yet. Not even close. This is not a finished product nor should it be advertised as one. It hasn't even been optimized yet. It is a bloated, buggy, incomplete mess, but at the same time it is a gem in the rough.
Unfortunately gems in the rough aren't worth much. They need to be polished first. GalCiv3 is lacking any and all polish. For comparison, I'd say that Dwarf Fortress has fewer bugs and is more stable than GalCiv3. Dwarf Fortress feels more polished than GalCiv3.
Thats right. You heard me right.
is a more polished, stable, and bug-free game than GalCiv3.
So if you're a die hard 4x fan and want another 4x game regardless of how unfinished it is, by all means, pick up GalCiv3. Just be prepared to forgive a lot of problems with the game. You're going to have to overlook a lot of issues with the game.

UPDATE: The devs have been hard at work so far on this game so I have updated this review for my current opinion. Earlier I recommended the game but to buy later when stuff was fixed, well lots of it has been fixed really fast since release.
UPDATE 2: My DLC concerns are out of the window as of May 5th 2015 due to the next two monsters being free for current owners of the game, and the price will go up for new buyers by $1 per monster which really isn't that bad at all. More fixes and balancing was done, and a free skin for the first monster was given free to current Steam owners until May 8th. The game is a much smoother experience and is coming along nicely and at a good rate. I'm actually surprised, being so cynical about the current state of the gaming industry it's really rare to see devs do so good and honestly makes me more than glad I bought this game on release day. The issue I had with 'depth' isn't as bad as it may sound if you read my original review below, but when I said 'deeper than it looks but not deep enough'  I want to revise that to 'deeper than it looks and deep enough for most'. Original review below for those still reading.
Original review:
I do recommend this game but there is a few caveats (UPDATE: 100% recommend the game at this point to anyone who would ask). It is deeper than it looks but not deep enough in some spots (UPDATE: revised above in my 2nd update of this review). It's like a reverse XCOM in the sense that you are trying to destabilize the world instead of save it, but you only have one base to operate from. That is a way to describe it, it's almost like you are playing the alien side in the original XCOM with your hidden base and once found will be assaulted.
DLC are advertised and that bums me out since we might not get anything for free at a later date, that is enough to scare off many people because we all have seen how well that worked for Evolve (UPDATE: As of my 2nd review update above this is not a problem at all, and definitely nothing like Evolve). Maybe the devs will have a better DLC model, but most of the time DLC just bums me out from purchasing any at all. Still this game is easy to lose a time in as it is now. Gameplay is simple and satisfying, this game can work as pick-up and go where you smash a single city or for extended gaming sessions and to top it off this shouldn't require a powerful PC. A few bugs here and there, nothing bad found yet. They are getting squashed at a regular rate though. I will swear there is nothing quite like controlling a mecha-godzilla stomping around a city while drinking some beer, that is seriously some good times.
So while I do recommend this game I would tell anyone who asked to buy it if you really dig some vids that are out now and if you are on the fence then wait on a sale maybe but the price is still good (UPDATE: I'd tell anyone this is a good game experience at this point and is getting better, 100% recommended purchase) Since there will be DLC in a year or so we might see a DLC pack on sale or a GOTY edition. At this point the game could develop well or not, anymore you never know even with companies with good track records. But the price is good, $13 to start. Wait and see how these DLC roll out and see how many features get added, but the developers are doing very good on stabilizing and balancing the game in it's current state and the prospects for the future of this game are much better than others we have seen recently I shall not mention. If I were to go in the past for a do-over I'd still buy the game when I did, I call it a good purchase for myself. (UPDATE: Game is being taken care of, bugs and glitches are being squashed at a fast pace and additions are being made in a fast manner and I consider this one of my better game purchases so far in 2015)

Like most sales pitch videos on Steam, Mission Control: NanoMech's avoids showing much gameplay.  The tags indicate it is an action RPG.  It has some RPG aspects, but it's really closer to a tower defense game.  Specifically, it is an active tower defense game, where you play a character that runs around the map placing towers and can be killed by the waves of enemies you have to destroy before moving on.
The educational aspect of the game is very poorly integrated with the gameplay.  The experience is similar to going to a university class on nanotechnology, and half paying attention while playing games on your cell phone.  The tower defense portion of the game is almost completely independent of the nanotech-related content.  The nanotech portion of the game is handled much like a presentation, with some minimal interactivity.  Completing some task in the tower defense portion starts the nanotech portion, then completing that gives you something new to use in the tower defense portion (e.g. a new tower, armor, or direct attack).  Performing well in the game does not require you to understand anything about nanotech.
From a game design standpoint, this is a bad choice.  A puzzle game like
,
, or
would have been a much more natural fit for the subject matter.
Ignoring the educational aspect and evaluating it purely as an active tower defense game, it's bad.  There are so few places you can place towers, and so few towers to choose from, that there is usually only one way to complete an area, and it is usually obvious (typically filling all slots with the most powerful tower you have, starting near the enemy spawn points).  The RPG aspects are very shallow, with no significant choice in your build.  Other bad design decisions abound, like the inclusion of walls that take time to disable, while providing no challenge, only increasing the time it takes to complete the game, and the amount of boredom and frustration.
Currently (November 2015) there is less than 3 hours of content.  That's counting the time taken by being required to rifle through lots of crates and wait for the timer on lots of walls to tick down to zero.
I'm not sure how NASA, the NSF, and Serious Play feel about having their names associated with this product, but if I were them, I'd be concerned.
There has been no news on or updates to this game since I purchased it almost a year ago, in December 2014, despite it being in Early Access.  It would appear the author has taken the money and run; not just the gamers' money, but the NSF's as well.
Please do not purchase this game.

Dust: An Elysian Tail is a masterpiece, plain an simple. The world of Dust is presented with amazing scenery and hand drawn and animated characters accompanied by beautiful music. You take control of an amnesic swordsman on a journey to discover himself and every character you meet along the way is voice acted and memorable. Not the least of is Fidget a character accompanies you the whole game and provides much of the game's needed comic relief. There is a real sense of joy as you uncover more of the story as you play, and help Dust learn more about himself (as well as hear what Fidget has to say about various encounters).
Gameplay wise Dust is a 2D metroidvania platformer. As you slice baddies you earn experience which you can use to improve your stats as you see fit and equip and craft items to further enhance your stats. Over the course of the game you and Fidget also gain further abilities to allow more freedom in not only disposing of your enemies but also reaching new areas. Apart from the main story there are a number of side-quests as well as hidden arenas to test your skill. And it is all a blast to play. I would really recommend a gamepad to play, especially an XBox 360 Controller.
The most impressive thing about Dust: An Elysian Tail is the fact that apart from the music, voice acting and part of the story, Dust was created, programmed and drawn entirely by one man,  Dean Dodrill. So in a way Dust is like an American equivalent of Cave Story. I know that may sound like a stretch, but honestly this game has brought me a lot of joy and fond memories and I would highly recommend this to anyone.

Full Disclosure: I backed the Indiegogo campaign and played the game prior to release!
Edit: Updated after the 1.03 patrol hotfix.
Updated Bit:
- You can now recycle unwanted buildings at your lair, and there are more tooltips for the secret base buildings.
- For those who were worried, volume sliders are in.
- Threatening cities (once you have built a properly dangerous reputation) is in, provided you build the proper base facility.
- Stupid play is still stupid play: Don't expect stomping only small apartment complexes to give you the resources you need. Tactical and strategic city-stomping is rewarded... time is a resource before city defenders show up, so go for the JUICY targets like universities, banks, and power plants.
- Core gameplay is in and solid. Technical issues (slowdown spikes on some rigs, very strong patrols) seem to have been addressed, but this game still has some rough edges. If you require prefect functionality, this game is not for you.
- Still an easy recommend if you are into city-stomping and varied monster training.
Pros:
- First Kaiju City Stomper/Base Building game in ages (ever?)
- Kaiju is not a static creature, but one the player nurtures and develops through resource gathering and training
- Training does not follow a fixed path! Game has 99+ abilities for the Kaiju, and the player is only expected to unlock around 33 on a normal run. Abilities are unlocked via a web, whereby you can't simply rush to the ability you want. Prereqs must be unlocked too.
- The world is not JUST your punching bag. Each region is building its own unique Kaiju to thwart you! There are six regions, each with a different mix of defense units.
- Resources! 5 you gather (Power, Knowledge, Money, "Organics", and Purpletonium) and one you can only spend- time! After five years of raiding and conquering, the Kaiju Defense Force is coming for you and your secret base.
- Unique city layouts! Each city is different and persistent, so the approach to optimally convert Caracas will be very different to the strategy needed for Seattle. Player decisions and needs matter and the game rewards considered city destruction. (Juicy targets may be mostly hidden behind terrain or skyrises, so there is an element of treasure hunting/Where's Waldo?)
- Base Building: The way you lose is if your secret Lair is destroyed, so you will need to build both defensive and production buildings to properly suceed. I don't have much experience with base defense yet, but you can make walls and at least 3 defensive turret types.
- Made by Kerberos Productions as an Indie! KP has a fantastic track record of support for their indie titles, both tech and free content. (Look at The Pit, their roguelike, which had numerous updates and tweaks in addition to expansions for over two years.)
- You get to stomp cities as a giant monster! Did I mention that? I think I did...
Cons
- Some sound effect kinks remain. The sound of tank tracks, for example, can play in the background even when you have left a city you are fighting.
- Kaiju control is very much "go there and bash things," no way to differentiate auto-attacks from just defenders or just buildings. This is a minor quibble though, as the player has pinpoint targeting control of most of the activated abilities you research. Can make the first few cities frustrating.
- Will not cure cancer.
Overall: A polished city-stomper with lots of variety and opportunities for skilled play to matter. All delivered in a quirky B movie style with lots of explosions. If you like this style of game, a wholehearted reccommendation!

This game wasn't quite what I expected.  It's one of those titles where the enemies are pretty tough & do a lot of damage, but are slow and telegraph their attacks.  Your character, on the other hand, is fragile and doesn't hit very hard, but can attack with great rapidity.  So, your only chance of winning (esp. on the higher difficulties) is to keep your foes stunlocked  with an all-out assault, chaining hits and special moves together to never give them an opening.  As I've stated before, I don't really like fighting games, where you have to pull off specific key combinations with millisecond timing.  This is pushing things a little, but I was still able to use the combos they had programmed in, which is fortunately not that many.  This does limit the depth of the system and mean the combats can get very same-y after a while, though.
So, it feels kind of incongruous.  Your protagonist is basically a walking abattoir, chewing through monsters with gusto.  Except he's also supposed to be a rabbit, I guess?  And all the other characters are cartoon animals too?  The story similarly veers back and forth between srs bzns and light-hearted banter. ABZU is an underwater adventure full of colourful environments and secrets below the surface. The deeper you explore the more of the truths you uncover in the depths. The game is stunning, immersive and just fantastic.

The small story is really touching. I really enjoyed it. Parts made it pretty linear which was slightly disappointing and I wish I had the ability to explore more. There were parts where I wished there were more to the story
Overall, I loved it. I recommend buying on a sale if you like value for your money. I say the average time would be 4 hours. If you want 100s of hours with solid gameplay, a gripping story or something more than this game then you are looking in the wrong place. [8/10 ]

It's a great turn based game, however i can't really recommend it as a casual buy.
Don't be fooled, there is no single player mode in this game, except for some little challenges that you do by your own, while waiting for other's turns (that's why those are made for);
This game, as you may have figured out, works by turns: you and your random-online opponent do some unit movements or actions within a set amount of possible moves, submit your turn, and wait for the other's one, and vice versa, till someone win the game by destroying his/her opponent's crystals or units.
That's it, a simple game, that i like as it is. But, you know, playing with random online people at this kind of game can sometimes ruin your fun... Infact, you won't know WHEN your opponent is going to make their next move, while you had done yours minutes ago (as for me, i tend to play with people that make their turns in a very long period of time, it means they do they move and straight close the game), bringing to the conclusion to find another opponent, hoping that in the while your previous opponent will reply, or that you may find at least a more responsive one.
Just this kind of gameplay may ruin the fun of the game, without the freedom to play this as much as you want to, and i would like to play this game more often than "a single move for each opponent, then swap to other games because i'm done here".
tl;dr: If you want to play this turn-based game, buy it only if you have a friend to play with.

Now don't get me wrong here, this game is fine.  It's just different from what I expected.
When I bought this game I was expecting some cool things like missions, custom games, and multiplayer.  Heck, maybe a couple different game modes.  Instead, I opened the game and the first thing I get is a tutorial shoved in my face that explains everything I could have figured out in two seconds.  Then it gives me a multiplayer option and a customization option.  Of course, I want to see what I can customize.
Originally, you can change your avatar and not much else.  Everything else is DLC.  Actually, everything in GENERAL is DLC.  You want to change your team color? DLC!  You want to play the other three team options?  DLC!  You want to play the mission mode I was ever so hoping for?  DLC!  You want to play the other game modes?  Well there arent any other game modes but if there was that would probably be DLC as well.  So after I realize that I can't play mission mode, I sigh and try to play multiplayer.  Since I enjoy TF2 quite a bit, I decide to go with that team instead of the other one that I have.
Well I start playing for like 30 minutes or so and I'm enjoying it.  There is a door at the bottom left with a turn number counting down.  I thought that was the amount of turns you had left before the game ended.  Nope.  It's how many turns you have left before you can surrender.  That's when I realize how LONG these games are.  They are like, really, really long.  Like, REALLY long.  Also, the learning curve is freaking gigantic.  90 minutes in I still don't know what in the heck half of my characters do.  And it seems like the teams you can buy are EXTREMELY overpowered.  I swarmed the guy with soldiers, demos a scout and a medic and in one turn one of his characters walked up and killed 3 of the 5.  It took me 3 turns to kill the character that did the deed.
But in the end, if you have the attention span of a goldfish like me and don't like having to buy DLC to get everything that the game promised I really don't recommend this.  Although if you like games like this, have patience and don't care about money, this game is for you.
Oh and one more thing: This game is an iPhone port and feels like an iPhone port.  Fair warning.

I'm going to be generous and recommend this game, with the SERIOUS caveat that you only bother buying it at a good sale price, and only if you really like inventory-based point and clicks and want to play a different one. The two main reasons for this are that it's incredibly short... And very, very easy--you can more or less complete it first time at the same speed you might in a second playthrough. I always mess about going back and forth all over games in my first playthroughs to see if there are Easter eggs to be found, even when it's so obvious what the next move is, and in this game it is always obvious, not just because the puzzles are easy, but they're also signposted in the dialogue.
Its good points are as follows:
- interesting storyline/nicely written, if a little (read a lot) derivative
- reasonable voice acting
- nicely drawn backgrounds
- a sense of vague mystery as to the identity of your protagonist
- a nice game to get the uninitiated into adventure games
So I'm ever the optimist, wishing to support adventure games wherever possible, especially indie efforts. But here are the cons, for the more initiated, which I'm afraid outweigh the pros and this part contains SPOILERS, so be warned:
- such a short game, I almost feel like I could have completed it within half an hour on my first try if I wanted
- very dissatisfying ending
- only two NPCs with which you can interact, and one of them doesn't talk. A third NPC is dead, if that counts
- the puzzles are so easy your average seven-year-old probably wouldn't struggle
- I've seen better background animation
- I've seen better characterization
- it's non-sale price is ridiculously high for what the game offers
- not a particularly original storyline
- protagonist walks so slowly, at least something that increases game time but one of my pet hates
- not many explorable areas
- hardly any meta (at most I think two observations per object)
- virtually nothing you can observe/comment on that's not essential to completion
- virtually no humour
- did I say this game is short and far too easy?
So I did enjoy it as an adventure-game hoarder, but can't recommend it to all. I do however, know how difficult it is to produce an adventure game, especially independently, and it is quite a polished effort when you consider that.

I might not have bothered with a pure visual novel, but this hybrid has convinced me that the genre is worth exploring.
Unfortunately, the production values seem low.  While I'm guessing that a lack of animation is expected within the genre, I would have liked better-fitting accessory overlays and perhaps some more character frames.  There were also instances where environment descriptions seemed to conflict with the relatively bland pictures.  On the bright side, only the mismatched overlays really bothered me as my first character is stuck with glasses that don't fit in her yearbook picture.
Honestly, it's an original English manga-styled choose-your-own-adventure book with middle school fantasy romance.  If you can stomach that description, the demo does a reasonable job setting expectations.

Belladonna is a short re-narration of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein presented in a classic Point&Click fashion.
By 'short' I mean it took me only 1.8 hours to complete the game.
Although the story is interesting it might make some players feel uncomfortable at times,
as it features a lesbian romance which involves the death of your former husband, the need to break open a sarcophagus and decapitating the corpse inside with a bonesaw, etc. What I personally disliked the most, is that you have to kill a cat in order to proceed...
Aside from that Belladona is quite an enjoyable experience. The difficulty is easy, as most of the puzzles are very straight-forward and require just a minimum of logical thinking. So the game felt more like an interactive storybook to me than a classical point&click adventure, a fact that I liked. The voice acting was great, too, as it suited the main character especially well. The plot is transported through various notes scattered around the game environment, while being perfectly fine to me, some players might prefer the story to be shown to them...
What I also noticed is, that the spelling of some characters' names is not consistent,
meaning that the same person is sometimes called 'Franziska', another
time it's 'Franzeska'. Not sure if I got something wrong there, though...
So, if you are looking for a decent but short adventure (and if you can cope with the above-mentioned twists), this is a game for you!

OK so if you've always wanted to decimate a city with  giant robot monster, this is the game for you.
A few things I didn't expect going in:
1) The level of detail. In terms of managing your secret base, upgrading and repairing your kaiju, there is a lot to do and consider.
2) How much actual fun causing mayhem in a seemingly helpless city is.
3) Level of difficulty. It's not quite as easy as it seems either. Cities will ramp up their efforts to repel you as you tear down more and more of their infrastructure (why are they so hostile?). So expect infantry, combat jeeps, tanks, helicopters and more to try to take a piece out of your precious Kaiju.
Apart from the aforementioned stuff, the art style and attention to detail in the layouts of the cities is very fitting and well-done. Who doesn't like goofy mad scientists bent on world destruction?
To summarize: Get this game if you want a casual, yet deep strategy experience that you can easily play in small bites or marathon sessions. It's strangely addicting. Just don't cackle in glee with your friends or family around. They...probably won't understand... Anyway, just get this game. You won't regret it.
P.S. Did I mention the X-Com like world map and  time compression system? I'll do that next time.

Voice acting is spot-on (every single line in the game is voiced), and the story is fantastic if a bit dark, with lots of comic relief scattered about. The gameplay is also very fun, mixing hack n' slash elements with metroidvania. Expect lots of combos, finishing moves and counterattacks. There's even an easy difficulty for anyone that isn't too good at these types of games, and a couple high difficulty modes for those who prefer a bigger challenge.
My only complaints might be that the bosses are a bit underwhelming, and that the crafting system is almost pointless. Bosses can be easily stunlocked and are ultimately big bags of HP, and the crafting system, while useful for upgrades, isn't really worth doing since you'll likely find a better, already-crafted item in a chest a few minutes after finding a crafting blueprint.

(Note: I played this game a lot more outside of Steam. Also unlike other 2.5D shooters, this is one that I didn't when I was young so there is no nostalgic feeling biassing me)
This game is the epitome of 2.5D shooters. Big, interactive levels, some of them are really really nice and atmospheric. A huge list of weapons with alternative fire modes and some quirky properties (your standard peashooter gun, isn't wat it seems at first). Gore, explosions, physics, you name it.
For first time players, it will probably feel a bit difficult (the highest dificulties are actually for co-op modes). But when you learn which weapon is the best for the current job, you'll get into the flow of the game and it's hugely satisfying.
Pro's:
- Very satisfying arsenal of weapons with alternative modes (and akimbo)
- Graphics (well yes, this isn't a DirectX 12 game, but the sprites really are top notch for games that old)
- Some of the coolest enemies to hunt down (CRUDOX CRUO!)
- Awesome, very fitting soundtrack
- Good (anti-hero) protagonist with a lot of funny lines
- Abundance of secrets and easter eggs (as it should with shooters from that era)
- A lot of gore
- Physics (kicking heads)
- Good dosbox port. I know some people state otherwise, but in my experience everything works as it should. I play WASD + mouse and after configuring my keys everything works.
Cons:
- You can't seem to turn down the music volume, which is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥in levels with carnival music.
- While some levels are superb, a few levels feel tedious (but this is like 1%)
- 6 different keys might be a bit overboard instead of the classic 3 keys
- Story (if you care about that stuff, I didn't)
- Unsatisfying end boss
I would give it 85%: must play

First off, I'm a huge Souls fan, just like most people here. I've logged over 1000 hours in the souls series and soulslikes, so I'm no stranger to the genre.
Recently, I've been playing a lot of established and up-and-coming roguelikes with success. Needless to say, I was stoked for Necropolis.
I'm a few hours in, and am loving every minute of it. The combat is not copy-pasted from Souls; it is a bit slower in some ways, but the elements are all there and solid. You'll be punished for being reckless. If I had to change anything about the combat, it'd be that you can't use a scroll mid-combat.
The long and short of it:
Pros:
Funny dialogue (think Portal's GLaDOS)
Solid gameplay, including
Difficult and rewarding combat (enemies ALWAYS drop their gear)
Randomly generated landscape
Extremely different landscape at each descending level
Movement is smooth; it isn't too slow when backtracking
Cons:
Scroll use is slow (many have in-combat one-time uses)
No tutorial (I'm left with many questions on classes)

I love this game, Its not really a game you sit down and play, Its more of a game you leave running in the background while you work / do other things, as you only really play for 10 seconds every few hours, unless you get an opponent on at around the same time as you.

I run about 10+ games so I always have some moves to play when I open up the game.
Some players Make there move instantly (takes about 30 seconds to update) some play a move every few hours/days
You can replay players and setup multiple games with players
This game is also an APP on Mobile devices, and you can share your account across them.

About people taking exception to the Steam port. They are mostly wrong.
Steam version contains:
- movies;
- CD-Audio tracks in OGG (emulated, so no CD needed in drive);
- AWE32 + Wave Blaster emulation out-of-the-box;
- original Setup.Exe program;
- predefined DosBox configuration files that can be manually launched.
SO you actually CAN run the Setup.Exe, change the resolution to VESA 2.0 and stop yelling it is only 320x200...
1. Open "Run..." dialog (press windows key +R)
2. Paste the
following line into the textbox:
=====
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\One Unit Whole Blood\dosbox.exe" -conf "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\One Unit Whole Blood\dosboxBlood_setup.conf" -noconsole -c "exit"
=====
3. Click OK.
When you find your favourite configuration, back-up the BLOOD.CFG file. When Steam reverts your changes to the original, you can fix it easily then.
I hever heard about official 3DFX support for Doom II or Blood. Steam version contains original software graphics engine.
And this is the freaking ADVANTAGE, because all new-gen fan-made ports break the gameplay experience (no offence at all, you may try them with Steam game files)!
I encountered no emulation lags on my old laptop. If you yell that game released in 1997 never gets 500FPS under emulated environmnent, you are IMO an id#ot, sir!
And you CAN change the controls, every single action has up to 2 keys! You can even set-up controls in a way to emulate the modern WSAD&mouse style, including mouse sensitivity adjustement. The only con is that mouse can aim only horizontally using standard config, but it is DOOM II-style. You can swim up-down using jump-crouch keys.
I don't even start talking about multiplayer mode (needs some effort to set up) and custom maps...
The only disadvantage is that there are no launch menu, but I needed to call Setup.Exe only a few times.
OVERALL: 1997/10! Would kick skeleton's head again!

Spintires amazed me when I first played it as a tech demo (2013?), beautiful graphics and a great physics simulation complete with deformable mud and realistic water all running smoothly on whatever crappy machine it was I had back then.
Now, several years have passed and some sort of conflict has erupted between the genius who made it (Pavel) and his publisher (Oovee).  Various promises have been broken and/or lies told.
This conflict continues as Pavel has a new publisher (Focus Home Interactive) and is releasing an update to Spintires under the name Mudrunner: A Spintires Game.  Again, various promises have been made, but they are a bit vague about what exactly is new (aside from new vehicles).  Oovee are not completely out of the picture and we don't know exactly what deal was made.  I'm also concerned about the game having had a "time bomb" put in by Pavel at one point, which made the game unplayable for those who owned it.  That doesn't really inspire trust.
Because of the above, I cannot recommend purchasing Spintires.  If you choose to believe Pavel, buy Mudrunner.  I'm on the fence, despite being entitled to a 50% discount as I own Spintires.  The new publisher is a good one - look at the mod support in Farming Simulator 2017, and their continued support for older titles such as Blood Bowl.

Cubic is a nice, short and casual puzzle game that has nothing new to offer but yeah, it's well realized and although it has its flaws, in my opinion deserves to be played if you like minimalistic logic games.
It's also quite easy, although I had to look at the great guide we have here on Steam for some directions xD
The game's available both in English and Russian, but you can stick with English even if you don't know it - I'm just telling this 'cos if you have foreign Steam clients like me, you'll have on the game store page a red rectangle saying that the game's not available in your language (Italian in my case) - 'cos there's literally no text in the game xD
The mechanics are very simple and it's short, mainly due to the little number of levels (only 16) 'cos as I said they, taken one by one, can be quite difficult in one way or another.
The game takes place on a colorful 3D field and as the title says you're a cube, that can be moved either with directional or WASD keys - thank God! Many games don't come with WASD support or they don't have the option to remap your controls and that's quite a pain for a long-time PC player!
Every level will have in the upper right side of the screen a required step number - if you reach 0 it's game over, another glimpse of difficulty - and there's a simple but somehow nice soundtrack. Ok, it gets monotonous after two minutes, being honest.
Unfortunately, I don't know exactly why but the achievements unlock only when you close the game. It's a bug (?) that other games have too, maybe it's related to a developing thing, I don't know.. as of the end of 2017 it hasn't been fixed so you won't get achievements on beating a level, but you'll get them when you'll close the game itself (so for the Russian achievement you won't earn it by changing the language in game and stop, you'll need to close everything too).
But let's go back to the game!!
The goal of every level is to connect color tiles and destroy them in a set number of moves. Going deeper, you'll be with your cube on a game board and every square will be colored of a single bright color. By stepping on the red square for instance you'll be red-colored and you'll need to step on another red-colored block in order to get them both white, until the whole game board has been de-colorized.
As I said it can be quite difficult, since you can't go around the board but you've got a limited number of moves to do everything :) On the other side, since this game has only 16 levels it's also short once you try and retry again the same level :)
Of course, the "emptied"/"whited" blocks will be free and you'll be free too to pass on them without losing your color, in order to get to the same-colored block you detected as your goal.
As a funny addition, you'll have always on the left side a "sample" of the blocks you have to eliminate, and their height is proportional to the number of blocks to destroy. That reminded me A LOT of Dr. Mario on the Game Boy.. which I still play today xD
What else can I say? It comes for the minimum price, 0,99€, and I bought it on sale while many other players bought it with a -90% coupon so I really think that spending two hours here (or less if you're smarter than me, and you don't leave open games while you're called to work in the neighbouring town and so on) is completely OK.
There are free to play games that deserve their 1€/$ and there are games that are way overpriced; this one requires the cheapest amount on Steam, 1€, and it completely met its expectations. Ok, maybe not the "extraordinary mechanics" that the main page offers to us but hey, it's a good simple logic game and everyone loves them xD
Although short, offers its challenge and meets its expectations so it's definitely recommended, it will take some hours of your time and entertain you as long as you like puzzle games of any sort :)
Feel also free to play it windowed and with a low quality, it runs smoothly and doesn't need much else! :)

Wow. This was oddly refereshing. Even though it's short and it doesn't last for very long, Cubic does a dang good job of being a puzzle game. It's simple, but not too complex. It's just the right amount to keep me invested and the right amount to keep me on a short limit. A brainteaser like this one is pretty decent all things considered. The graphics aren't much, but they aren't the game's strong aspects. The gameplay is where it shines the most. You are a cube standing on colored tiles trying to match one tile with another of its respective color. Standing on another tile when you are already a different color just makes you that color, but standing on a tile with the same color clears those tiles from the set. You have a limited amount of steps and the only real change to gameplay is the small portals which is easy to understand. They teleport you to the corresponding portal and you don't get changed in color, just moved in position. This works well as most of the core gameplay is still there, but isn't so far off that you'd be confused. In my mind, if you get this for free or on sale, it's generally worth it.
Pros:
-Gameplay is easy to understand and isn't too hard to grasp a hold of. It works for this short game.
-Graphics are simple, but they do the intended purpose well. It shows what color you are, when the colors disappear when you match two of the same colored tiles, and where the exit and portals are.
-Soundtrack is okay. It can drone on, but seeing as the game can be completed under an hour, it isn't an issue.
Cons:
-The trading cards are currently unavailable. Not sure why this is, but you won't get the trading cards currently from this game.
-Achievements are very easy to unlock. If you are the kind of person that likes a challenge, this game isn't for you. There's only a total of about 16-20 levels and they can be easily be completed in under a minute or under 10 minutes.
Overall Rating: I'd give Cubic a good solid 5/10 or a 6/10.
Comments: While it is short that makes me want more, I ultimately like that they didn't go further as it feels as though it would have been negated heavily by the sheer amount of levels if they added more. It's good for achievement hunters and people who have a little money to spend on a game. It was worth my time of 40 minutes or more to finish the game.

It has potential, that's for sure.
My main complaints is:
-The amazingly stupid sector management AI which can't even put slaves and robots in the correct tiles. They keep putting them to farm energy credits and research points while ignoring the fact that slaves and robots (except synthetics) have disadvantages to farm it.
-Non-existent diplomacy. It's so simple it hurts. Declare war, trade resources, declare rivalry, insult them. Just that. As for the casus belli for war, currently the choices are very limited. Giving only 3 choices; cede planet, vassalize, or liberate some of their planets.
The only part I definitely love playing is the early-game stage, you'd be surprised at what events the game will throw at you when you start to explore the galaxy.
The mid-game? It's your average Europa Universalis IV, but imagine it without any DLC. Yeah, that's it. Here's what you do during mid-game:
-Build ships.
-Wait for your tech research to complete.
-Upgrade your ships with the latest weapons you acquired from research.
-Declare war.
Rinse and repeat, since there's no other thing except warring other states to "win" this game.
Late-game stage is bugged. Foreign invaders? Sure thing, the AI doesn't even fight them! Except for Fallen Empires, that is. I still remember when the Unbidden appears, it only gave opinion bonus to all AI states, making them forming federation here and there. But because of that federation, they won't declare war to each other since they're locking each other. That creates a horribly static galaxy which nothing happens, even when Unbidden starts swallowing those states, they don't do anything!
Then again, it's not like I hate this game or something, but currently it feels like an incomplete game. Perhaps in a year or so, when PDS releases some DLCs for this it'll be as good as CK2 or EU4, or even Vicky 2.

One thing I'll mention at the start is that there is a spoiler at the end of this review, I wouldn't usually but I'm pointing out a massive flaw in the story, so it's somewhat unavoidable.
Ultimately, the game is cheap, and as I got it in a bundle it cost me pennies, so I can't really hate it. For the price, it's probably about what I'd expect. It's a nice way to kill time for an hour, and once you start playing, you'll want to finish purely to confirm that your guess is correct regarding what happened. That doesn't mean it deserves a recommendation though.
The biggest problem I had with the game was the length. You can probably complete this in an hour, or 2 if you're like me and a) can't see for toffee and continually walk past one of the items tens of time, and b) spend half of it looking for secrets, of which there are none. The story progresses very quickly, and although it's interesting, it loses points for it's inability to keep you in anticipation of the ending. Not even half way in, and you can guess easily enough what happened.
It also isn't difficult. I didn't read anything about the game when I started, so I wasn't too sure what I was getting myself into, but I expected jump scares and hiding from a murderer or something along those lines, but there's none of that. There are technically puzzles in it, but they are so obvious that they require no thought. The items are easy to find, (though there was one that I just couldn't notice for a while), so most of them you're likely to have picked up on your way through already, so there isn't a lot of back tracking like you would expect for a game like this. The entire area you can explore is very small as well.
Another big one for me was the voice acting. The voices didn't match the characters, and they truly sounded staged. I don't know who did the voices, but it sounded like they picked someone random from the street, or perhaps the game makers used their own voices. It was off putting.
The ending was also rushed. You'll have everything already once you get the final objective, with the exception of one item which is already explained to you how to get, so you don't even need to work for it. You get them, do the thing, and it's suddenly over. The ending truly was not satisfying at all.
One thing I did like was the artwork, it suited the story quite a lot, though it could have been animated a lot better.
It's unfortunate that the ending wasn't really set up for a continuation, at the length it is it'd be better if it was just one chapter of a larger story. This game would be vastly improved if they increased the playing time, added a lot more exploration, added some difficult puzzles, and perhaps a mad murderer you had to avoid to keep you on your toes.

There was one thing that bugged me in this. You get a key from the dead body of the husband. The key unlocks a box containing another key. That key is used to wind up the wife. The wife says the reason she couldn't wind herself up is because the key on her back is placed out of her reach, so only someone else can wind her up. This suggests that she had access to the key. Then why did she lock it up and put the smaller key on the husbands body, whome she hated? It makes no sense. It'd perhaps make more sense if she just changed the line to: "I couldn't wind myself up because I didn't have access to the key", but if she had time to do the experiment, wouldn't she at least have time to look for the key on the corpse?
And since I'm spoiling anyway, there's another annoying thing about the story. The maid wrote a note suggesting she was falling out of love with the wife, but if you try to mention it to the wife, she decides against telling it in the end. If you put something like that in, you should at least expand on it, otherwise it feels completely pointless. Even just a simple alternative ending, like a good ending if she stays quiet, and a bad ending if she doesn't. With the ending being just one still image, all that needs to be done would have one more image as an alternative, and it'd tie up a lot nicer than it currently does.
Anyway, that's my review of the game, I'll won't be recommending it, but honestly if it's on offer for a quid or part of a bundle or something, they I'd at least consider it.

The game has a single Kaiju in it now, a Mechagodzilla inspired robozilla, and down the road they'll release at least two more - maybe more. It works, it's fun, and it's the only game like it... so it's a pretty easy $12ish to spend.

Unfortunately I can't recommend this game.
Being a huge fan of Journey, I am knew I was going to compare this game to thatgamecompany's masterpiece. And that's a large part of why this game didn't work for me.
It's a very pretty game, with pleasant music and impressive visuals. But to me, that's all it is. There is very little gameplay to speak of, and I honestly thought I would *like* it for that reason, but I didn't. There is such a thing like too little gameplay, and in my view, this game is guilty of it.
To some extend, Abzu is a shallow copy of Journey, only it leaves out the essential co-op that made Journey such a profound game. When I first played Journey, I was sucked right into the mood. This game doesn't do that for me. It is a stark reminder as to the importance of good game design. If anything, this game feels like a shallow, surface-level clone of some of Journey's moments. It utterly fails to capture that game's essence, and only replicates a surface understanding of what made Journey great.
I still hold Matta Navis and Austin Wintory in very high regard. They both excel at what they do, but next time they should involve some game designers too!

You can see it in the screenshots, but Dust is a beautiful game. The art is beautiful. The music is beautiful. The gameplay is beautiful. The story is... well, I wouldn't say "beautiful" but it's definitely interesting. I only have a few things I didn't like about this game.
1) It's short. I got 114% complete (all items and map exploration) in about 10 hours on normal. If you play on a higher difficulty, your experience may be different. I found normal to be not too much of a challenge, though I did "die" twice (I had revival stones though, so I came right back to life). Post game content is none unless you didn't collect or do everything before beating the game.
2) The portraits are a little fuzzy around the edges, and the few animated cut scenes there are seem to be in 480p rather than HD. However, this didn't detract from my overall enjoyment of the game or the cut scenes.
Extra Pros worth mentioning:
1) The voice acting is great. Fidget's voice is kind of annoying, but it fits her, so not too many complaints about that.
2) Controller support is great. It feels very natural, includes rumble, and overall plays like a console game. I never used the keyboard, so I can't attest to the quality of that, though the keys are customizable.
3) There are a lot of graphical tweaks you can set in the options to improve performance or "increase immersion" depending on the strength of your computer and preference.
I got this during the summer sale and couldn't be more pleased. I might not have paid $15 for this game given how short it is, but I'd definitely pick it up if it goes down to $10.

The Witcher 2 is an amazing RPG with a great story! It is very different to other RPGs in that way that the main emphasis doesn't lie on grinding for better gear, but telling a story wich is greatly influenced by your decisions. You are often confronted with the choice between two sides or decisions over life and death. Many of these actions taken will have an influence on what happens later in the story. On one occasion there is even a small difference based on a choice you made in the first witcher game if you have played it.
I like the Witcher 2 very much for its great atmosphere and the story which keeps a couple of surprises in store for the player. Also you have different possibilities for your fighting style. Depending wether you prefere the classical close combat swordsmanship or using signs (the magic spells in the Witcher). If you want to really go in deep you can also improve your abilities by using alchemy and self-brewed potions which then gives you many options to react to the enemy you are facing.
I can highly recommend this game to everyone who enjoys a good story which reacts to your made decisions and has an easy to learn fighting system which feels very dynamic.

While not an actual game in itself, Lost Coast originally started as one of the intended levels to be included in Half-Life 2, but their designs took another path and this level would have been left by the wayside. Instead, they creative repurposed this map to showcase various elements of the Source Engine and the technology and effects it can support. Various comment bubbles are strewn about to allow you to selectively listen to, and in many cases view, commentary related to a particular aspect or visual. Not a game, but an interesting and interactive documentary that will allow you to learn more about the engine and their mentality when designing many of the maps and environments of the game. Give it a try at least once, seriously.

Necropolis is in itself a really cool concept for a co-op roguelite. It has really nice art direction, visuals and the music is great too, sadly that's where most of the positive things about it ends.
The first thing I noticed when I started the game was that you couldn't rebind any of the keys. For a left handed player that's not a great first impression at least it has controller support though (be noted that users are currently experiencing certain issues using Xbox controllers, I however never had any troubles with it).
As soon as you pick a character to play the game throws you abruptly into its dark and mysterious world. You aren't told anything from start, instead you have to uncover the underlying lore as you progress. The narrator (The Brazen Head)) also helps you and talks in the background while you progress.

The dialogue and quotes the game feeds you with are of the humorous and random kind, I personally didn't like it, in some cases it felt too out of place. This mainly comes down to personal preference so it's not necessarily a negative, other people might like it much better than me.
When it comes to optimization however there's much to ask for, it's horribly optimized and full of bugs. Enemies will spawn inside walls or walk through walls, items will drop inside walls, collision detection needs more work and so on.
I've got a high end PC but I had to turn down specific graphic settings for it to run at an OK frame rate. Game kept freezing/stuttering at times when loading in new areas/items/monsters and pop-in were an issue at times too. I can live with the pop-ins, but the game needs to be optimized.
The combat being the main draw for this game was a big letdown, both clunky and lacking, combining it with the lack of re-bindable keys didn't help either. I highly recommend using a controller, it's far better than playing with keyboard and mouse (at least for now).
The combat could potentially be improved upon by adding certain visual and audio cues so that the player understand what is going on and where attacks are coming from. When 10 enemies swarm you from all directions it's not easy to keep track of what's going on, especially when you're in a dark room.
Enemy AI could also be improved, I saw several cases of enemies standing inside each other or walking blindly into walls. Enemies also wouldn't attack me attack me at times because I stood behind a crate or some other small object.
The pacing during the first area is a bit too slow for my liking, luckily it becomes much better later on as you've unlocked new items and managed to get better gear. A map or a minimap would also have been very helpful, it's easy to get lost in the maze like levels that all look alike. Maybe you can unlock or find one later on, but I've not managed to do so.
I really want to love this game, great concept but very rough around the edges. It's apparent that it needs a few more months of extra polish to iron out all the problems, if so then it'll actually be a really good game. Sadly I can't recommend it in its current state because of this.

There are 3 different Build Engine games that really count: Duke Nukem, Blood, Shadow Warrior. They all basically play the same in that you are a smartass with lots of interesting and bizarre weapons going level to level, massacring everything in your path and collecting keys to progress.
Blood is the horror one of these three for sure. The game's plot is basically cult member who got screwed over by a demon is reborn and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off. The protagonist is just as clever and enjoyable as Lo Wang or Duke and personally my favourite of the three.
The weapons are quite fun and you really do feel like a sadist when you light up people with a flare gun and they scream like mad. It fits the protagonist's character extremely well.
The level design is not as frustrating in regards to key hunting. I never needed a FAQ or to even look at the map though some secrets are really hard to find.
The game is quite long I feel and there are 5 difficulty levels so you don't ever rage quit because of it being too difficult.
It is packed with horror references from films and books even in the tiniest places. The protagonist is also quite witty and the voice acting is really cool. For younger gamers some of these will go over their heads since they didn't grow up reading Lovecraft or watching Phantasm for example. But as a 28 year old gamer I am constantly chuckling at the various references.
Also, it has numerous mods available.
All in all I think if you enjoy the Build Engine games then you will enjoy Blood but it is a great plus if you are an older horror fan.

American-made visual novel that follows Japanese archetypes.
Is not perfect but deserves your support. A small single-man production company producing a VN with a long running time (one run is about seven hours) with dozens of choices, all which effect other choices, with dozens of ways to both fail and succeed that utterly change how the story plays out each time you go through. I've clocked at least eight ways the game can end so far, with a hundred smaller details mixed into those endings.
Experience is marred by none of the characters having truly standout personalities, and a visual style that will be hit-or-miss for you.
But given the price, the one man production team, and the overall quality of the product its still a hit more than a miss. And one of the few true VN's with branching paths that English-only speakers can get their hands on.

Cubic is a short, simple and cheap grid-based puzzle game that can be finished in around an hour. I discovered this game through a 90% off coupon which means I didn't have high hopes for this game but it was much more fun than I was expecting it to be. The goal of each level is to get rid of all the coloured floor tiles by stepping on two tiles of the same colour in a row in a certain number of moves. This is a pretty interesting idea that I haven't seen in any other game and the puzzles were decent - I got stuck on a few of them for a while, but I beat many of them on my first try without thinking about them.
I feel like there is more that can be done with this concept (the only real new element brought in is teleporters) but for the price you're paying I would say that it's worth it. For me it was worth it since I got it for £0.08!

This point and click game is a rather unique recreation of 'Frankenstein or The Modern Prometheus' by Mary Shelley with all the thought provoking moral and ethical drama of the original.  This game is a STORY; heard through the poignant remarks and observational thoughts of the lead character and (OMG the horror) READ through journal notes.  There are 18 notes total, 9 by Dr. Wolfram von Trauerschloss (Trauerschloss means Mourning Castle in German) 5 before and 4 after the reanimation of his wife, 4 by his wife, Belladonna while she was alive, 4 by Belladonna after she is reanimated, and 1 by her faithful servant, Klara Seiber.  Part point and click, part visual novel, part walking simulator, part horror, part mystery, part commentary and ALL ABOUT THE STORY BEING TOLD from different perspectives and points of view.  That is tough to do in only 18 journal pages and those 18 pages get the job done, and done very well.
Most reviewers state that this is a short game and it is.  I finished in 119 minutes (and I am slow) but was quite satisfied by the story told.  It was like reading a short story or novella.  The end was a bit truncated I thought and not seemingly appropriate until thought about.  Yet how else could it have ended but the way it did.  The epilogue is a single screenshot the credits play over, and picture shows everything that needs to be stated.
Reviewers complain about having to READ.  Really? Seriously?  18 handwritten journal pages are too much??  And 1 has only a few words on it.  Plus the questions/dialogue near the end that explains so much motivationally, ethically, and morally. That was too much to read??? (Sighs in disbelief and shakes head).
There are no puzzles.  (Really there are none despite other reviewers saying there are.)  It is a straight linear STORY with little inventory that reveals itself and characters as the game progresses.  It is not even an adventure but it had to be put is some category other then horror, I suppose.
Worth the READ because this game is more of a STORY than anything else.

You wake up as a reanimated corpse in a laboratory with no memory of who you are or what has happened: you set out to uncover your identity and, reading a journal page you find nearby, you start to uncover the sad, sordid story of the place.
Belladonna is a very short point and click adventure with gothic and dark elements sporting a good story but sadly lacking in gameplay and length.
-the dark art style is quite good
-atmospheric sound design backed up by an eerie soundtrack
-good voice acting
-the journal pages you find around are well written and eventually shed light on a good story of love, loss and betrayal
-puzzles are extremely easy, their solutions are also often spoon-fed through item descriptions
-very short, expect 45/60 minutes
Belladonna is a mixed bag overall: its story is pretty good and slowly uncovering what happened and who you are by reading through journal pages is an engaging, albeit short-lived, process. Puzzles, on the other hand, are so easy and straightforward that the gameplay suffers as a consequence, there just isn't any challenge.
I do feel the well written story is worth a playthrough though, hence my thumbs up: I'd avoid paying full price due to the basic gameplay and short length but when on sale or in a bundle it's a decent experience, think of it as an interactive gothic short story.

Ok, so, not sure where to start with this so I guess GAMEPLAY: The gameplay is a 2D platformer with some brawling type elements in it, along side some unique (I think) Twists, such as the Dust Storm. The Dust Storm on it's own is nothing too powerful, but when combined with any of the powers aquired for fidget, (Or the starting one, the poweres themselves are weak alone as well) they become much more powerful and extreamly useful in the combat. The only complaint I can thing of is that I could not get the timing of how to parry down that easily, but I did eventually get it, and it is almost required to defeat some of the enemies... The difficulty of the game is not that hard if you are decent at gaming, so I would reccomend going on to one of the harder difficulties to add some challange and fun to the experience. VISUALS: The visuals in this game are just GORGEOUS, The hand painted scenery is just beautiful to look at. The characters are Anthromorphic (Which for people whom may not know, is a animalstic human, as if taking the features that are commonly associated with animals and applying them to a humanoid body), which is actually an unique thing that not a long of games ever do, because they are afraid of losing sales due to people having a bias SOLE REASON of people being aginst the art style and hating the normal type of art that people do in it. Which, I can understand as a reason to not want to attempt to try it because they need sales, but this game took the risk, and with it, the backlash that comes along with it, but they created what they wanted, and that just makes the game all the better. STORY (Spoiler Free!): The story begins out with you in a forest, with amnesia, then comes a FLYING talking sword and along with it a guardian who is lacking in skill at their job because, well, THEY LET THE SWORD FLY AWAY, anyway, the guardian is Fidget, and all the main characters of the game done, right there. Now off on an adventure to SAVE THE WORLD (Or maybe destory it? :P) ((Minor spoilers: You don't destroy the world)). Anyway, the moral of the story (Not saying what) is actually one that is rarely, if ever covered in games, and the ending is just perfectly exicuted in my opnion.  Anyway, to conclude this, guess I should give a score, since I loved this game so much, I have since first obtaining it obtained a total of 3 copies of it, soooo.... 11/10 Would fidget again.

The Witcher 2 is an amazing RPG with a great story! It is very different to other RPGs in that way that the main emphasis doesn't lie on grinding for better gear, but telling a story wich is greatly influenced by your decisions. You are often confronted with the choice between two sides or decisions over life and death. Many of these actions taken will have an influence on what happens later in the story. On one occasion there is even a small difference based on a choice you made in the first witcher game if you have played it.
I like the Witcher 2 very much for its great atmosphere and the story which keeps a couple of surprises in store for the player. Also you have different possibilities for your fighting style. Depending wether you prefere the classical close combat swordsmanship or using signs (the magic spells in the Witcher). If you want to really go in deep you can also improve your abilities by using alchemy and self-brewed potions which then gives you many options to react to the enemy you are facing.
I can highly recommend this game to everyone who enjoys a good story which reacts to your made decisions and has an easy to learn fighting system which feels very dynamic.
You can do whatever you want and its lots of fun with friends.

The Witcher 2 is the best RPG I have ever played. Not only that, it is probably my second favourite game of all time.
Why you ask?
Not only does the game treat you like an adult with non-censored mature content, but it also manages to immerse you into the extremely fantastic yet realistic world of the Witcher. But we're not done yet. The game also sports a complex and challenging combat system that only helps immerse you more into the world. As Geralt, you can't just run into a group of enemies with your sword and expect to come back alive. No, Geralt may be a Witcher, but he is also just a man. In order to dominate your opponents you'll need to prepare carefully for expected encounters by drinking potions. Potions that let you see your enemies through walls or strengthen you. Now let's talk about the story. As stated before, the game treats you like an adult and the story is a great example of that. It's not a simple tale of "going to save the world", this is a story of political intrique and rebellion. Paired with a large cast of interesting and three dimensional characters, you have your self one hell of a story.
But all said and done, you just want to know if you should buy it.
The definitive answer to that is yes.

I don't usually do reviews unless there's a very specific reason, or if I REALLY like a game. For me, Necropolis calls for both cases. Personally, I quite enjoy Necropolis, especially with friends that are into Roguelikes. The combat is slow, yes; to me, it's incredibly satisfying to be doing flips in the air as you land a fully-charged heavy attack on a group of Hoardmen. The environment is finely detailed, and where you can find it, lore's scattered throughout the generated rooms and halls in the forms of sorts of carvings and pictures, which sometimes open secret rooms. The farthest my friend and I have made it is level four, and we plan on going much farther. The only things I would complain about are the sometimes clunky animations for enemies and the wonky camera controls for keyboard and mouse users (using a gamepad), but both are avoidable for me.
I also feel that the amount negative reviews are doing this game an unfair injustice. I haven't seen a review by anyone that's played this game over two hours (which is fair for the most part, it's a $30 game, and that could be spent elsewhere), and I'd really like to hear someone's opinion that has gone through most of the game, and not just four levels consisting of two environments. Of course it's going to be boring, you've just touched the surface!
That being said, I like it. A lot. My friends and I will be playing plenty of it, but if you think about getting this, realize that to really experience it, you might not be able to in two hours.

This seems to be one of those where people go "oh it's got a message and an artistic style--SO SUBLIME" or "oh it has limited game mechanics--SO OVERPRICED."  Here's my take: it does have a message, but if you've already played World of Goo, you've already heard it.  Their messages are about as subtle as a strategic nuclear weapon, and they of course satirize culture, industrialization, and so forth.  One gets the feeling that these fellows would use the word "sheeple" in conversation without irony.
So grading it on what it intends to be, it does well.  The gameplay is casual and roughly amusing, and their sense of humor is bitingly sharp.  If you're right of center and sensitive, it'll probably tick you off.  Me, being the pinko that I am, find myself agreeing with its theses but not its attitude.  It's more than happy to point out flaws everyone knows about, but offers no solutions (nor does it really suggest that anything can be solved).  It's the "Folk Song Army" of message-driven computer games: well-intentioned and sweet-tongued but generally ineffectual and not particularly helpful.

On the surface Magical Diary appears to be just another text-based anime game, some kind of dungeon crawler, another paranormal school setting or a Harry Potter clone. YIELDMakes 4 servings ACTIVE TIME15 min TOTAL TIME2 3/4 hr
INGREDIENTS
1 (5- to 6-lb) Long Island duck (also known as Pekin)
2 cups boiling-hot water
1 tablespoon kosher salt
1 teaspoon black pepper
PREPARATION
Put oven rack in middle position and preheat oven to 425°F.
If necessary, cut off wing tips with poultry shears or a sharp knife. Remove and discard excess fat from body cavity and neck, then rinse duck inside and out. Prick skin all over with a sharp fork. Fold neck skin under body, then put duck, breast side up, on a rack in a 13- by 9- by 3-inch roasting pan and pour boiling-hot water over duck (to tighten skin). Cool duck, then pour out any water from cavity into pan. Pat duck dry inside and out, reserving water in pan, then rub duck inside and out with kosher salt and pepper.
Roast duck, breast side up, 45 minutes, then remove from oven. Turn duck over using 2 wooden spoons, and roast 45 minutes more. Turn duck over again (breast side up), tilting duck to drain any liquid from cavity into pan. Continue to roast duck until skin is brown and crisp, about 45 minutes more (total roasting time: about 2 1/4 hours). Tilt duck to drain any more liquid from cavity into pan. Transfer duck to a cutting board and let stand 15 minutes before carving. Discard liquid in roasting pan. thats it

Stellaris features multiple things that set it apart from its competitors:
1) Pause/play global action. All fights, events, exploration... everything in the game is real time pause/play! (no turns)
2) Unique research method of generating 3 options at a time (no tree).
3) Control not just one leader, but multiple leaders that serve under your main one(s).
4) Expand planetary building functionality as your population steadily expands across the planets.
5) The MOST EXTENSIVE character/faction creation system in this kind of game yet.
6) Unique art style, featuring ANIMATED 2-D character icons that work extremely well for the variety of races.
7) SOOOOOO many races! (With more surely to follow)
8) Unique planet types with habitation possible even in extreme conditions.
9) Unique alert system that compliments the pause/play global function well.
10) Extensive star systems and unique means of traveling between said systems.
11) Events that make mention of YOUR unique empire name (event mission chains of sorts).
12) Speed up and slow down time globally as you please. Want that research done now? High speed baby!!!
I am certain that there are more amazing things that I am either forgetting at the moment or have yet to encounter, but I am loving this game thus far. It is worth every penny that I spent on it, and I got the most expensive version! I can't wait to see what they have in store for the future DLC and steam workshop content that modders will add! I am also looking forward to checking out the art book and novel that were included with my purchase.
Verdict: 10/10 (will continue updating)
p.s. My only complaint isn't even really a valid complaint. I ordered the most expensive edition (forget what it was called) and was kindof hoping to receive physical copies of the novel, signed poster and perhaps the artbook. All of it was digital though. The most approachable of Paradox' games so far. It has a very useful in-game tutorial, clear interface.

This is a slow steam locomotive in terms of game pace: don't expect to get into proper warfare until you are a few hours in. You need all your early game resources to expand your economy, then expand by getting more colonies and protect them with a larger navy. The neutral creatures that roam the world provide interesting targets to shoot at, and the dozens of random events keep you busy while you slowly build your empire.
If you are new to 4X games or to Paradox games, this might be a good gateway drug for you.
